can_do_statement: Can put two noun phrases together (in apposition) to refer to the same person or thing, usually separated by commas.

ontology.mental_model: Two noun phrases side-by-side to define the same entity
ontology.pedagogical_hook: When you want to give more detail about a noun you just mentioned, you can add another noun phrase right after it, usually between commas.

positives: Mr Miller, the Sales Director, will visit us next Thursday.
A new employee, Mary Watts, has just joined our company.
negatives: Mr Miller will visit us next Thursday, and the Sales Director will come too.
A new employee has just joined our company, which is great.

can_do_statement: Can use the noun phrase 'The thing' in front position, with a clause complement, to give focus to something.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To highlight a specific point or aspect, start your sentence with 'The thing (that)...'

positives: The thing I enjoyed most about it was a new computer game.
The thing I prefer there is the swimming-pool.
negatives: I enjoyed the thing you gave me.
I prefer the swimming-pool, that is the thing.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with plural nouns + ' + noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: When a plural noun ending in 's' possesses something, you just add an apostrophe after the 's'.

positives: He had promised that he would go to his grandparents' house this afternoon.
Our company is a digital company with 15 years' experience.
negatives: He would go to his grandmother's house this afternoon.
Our company has 15 years of experience.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE '‘S' + NOUN
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with noun phrase + 'of' + noun phrase + possessive determiner ''s' + noun phrase.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: You can link two possessive ideas by using 'of' followed by a noun with an apostrophe 's'.

positives: I saw the window of my neighbour's car was broken.
The subject of my boss's talk will be IT skills.
negatives: I saw my neighbour's car was broken.
The subject of the talk will be IT skills.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with an indefinite pronoun + adjective or clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: When describing an indefinite pronoun (like something or nothing), the adjective comes after the pronoun.

positives: We see each other every day and do something different every day.
But then there is nothing special to eat.
negatives: We do different things every day.
There are no special meals to eat.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with noun + 'of' + possessive determiner + noun + '‘s', particularly with 'friend' or 'friends'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To show possession more elegantly, use 'a friend of my father's' instead of 'my father's friend'.

positives: The owner is a friend of my father's.
She is an acquaintance of my sister's.
negatives: The owner is my father's friend.
She is my sister's acquaintance.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with 'a friend of' or 'friends of' + possessive determiner + noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: You can describe relationships by saying 'a friend of' followed by a possessive determiner and a noun.

positives: He is a friend of my husband.
I thought they were friends of my neighbour.
negatives: He is my husband's friend.
I thought they were my neighbour's friends.

can_do_statement: Can form noun phrases with noun + 'of' + possessive pronouns.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a noun followed by 'of' and a possessive pronoun (like 'mine', 'yours', 'his') to indicate that it's one of many things belonging to someone.

positives: I told her lots of silly mistakes of mine.
I'm a fan of his, he is my favorite singer.
negatives: I told her lots of my silly mistakes.
I'm his fan, he is my favorite singer.

can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases by using adjective phrases as postmodifiers to give more information about the noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Sometimes adjectives come after the noun they describe, especially when the adjective is part of a longer phrase.

positives: We went to an island full of different and exotic species.
They delivered a box completely ready for shipment.
negatives: We went to a full island of exotic species.
They delivered a ready box for shipment.

guideword: FORM: NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE 'S WITHOUT NOUN
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with noun phrase + 'of' + noun phrase + possessive determiner ''s', omitting the noun where it is previously mentioned.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: If the noun is obvious from context, you can drop it after an apostrophe 's'.

positives: Our team is faster than our competitors'.
I think it would be better to include a student's view of the college, not only a teacher's.
negatives: Our team is faster than our competitors' team.
I think it would be better to include a student's view, not only a teacher's view.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADJECTIVES COMBINED WITH 'BUT'
can_do_statement: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with more than one adjective combined with 'but'.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To create a strong impression, you can use 'but' to link two contrasting adjectives before a noun.

positives: I was born in a small but beautiful city.
The smoke in the air had a strong but good smell.
negatives: I was born in a small city but it is beautiful.
The smoke was strong but good.

can_do_statement: Can use nominalised forms in academic or business contexts, to make something more formal.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: In formal or academic writing, turn verbs into nouns (nominalisation) for a more professional tone.

positives: The output in state-owned industry increased by 12%.
We noted the fluctuations in industrial output.
negatives: The industry produced state-owned items.
They fluctuated industrially.

guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH 'LITTLE OR NO'  + NOUN
can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with 'little or no' + noun.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: To emphasize that something is almost non-existent, use 'little or no' before a noun.

positives: They have little or no spare time to relax.
These blockbusters have little or no artistic value.
negatives: They have little time to relax.
There is no artistic value here.

can_do_statement: Can form complex noun phrases with 'wh-' cleft clauses, followed by 'be', to give focus.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Start a sentence with a 'What...' clause followed by 'is' or 'was' to place strong focus on the information that comes next.

positives: What everyone loved were the special effects.
What companies care about is money.
negatives: Everyone loved the special effects.
Companies care about money.

can_do_statement: Can use nouns and noun phrases as subjects of the clause.

ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use a noun or noun phrase at the beginning of a clause as its subject.

positives: His name is Stanislav.
My friends are from Poland.
negatives: It is raining today.
There are three apples.
